title: Sugarcane farms become the Tainan Science Park
actors: Executive Yuan; National Science Council; Taiwan Sugar Corp. (Taisugar)
what: The Executive Yuan decided in 1995 to create the Southern Taiwan Science Park. The Tainan campus was laid out on Taisugar's Daoye and Shanhua farms, about 1,038 ha. Phase II was approved in 2001, bringing Phases I–II to about 1,043 ha.
tension: State-held sugar land made fast assembly possible, so the park's first footprint came from converting agricultural estate land rather than buying from many small owners. Later expansions had to reach into private farmland.
outcome: Today the former cane fields host a cluster with over NT$1 trillion in annual sales; Phases I–II were about 99% leased by 2022, driving pressure for Phase III and beyond.
sources: Ministry of Culture, 南科考古館 article (2010) https://file.moc.gov.tw/001/Upload/OldFiles/AdminUploads/contenthistory/28-5.pdf | TechNews, 南科台南園區擴建 (Jan 2023) https://technews.tw/?p=1017344

when: Excavations from late 1990s; museum proposed 2002, approved 2007
title: 58 archaeological sites unearthed under the park
place: Tainan Science Park and adjacent industrial zones
actors: Academia Sinica (Institute of History & Philology); NSC; Tainan County Government; National Museum of Prehistory
what: Rescue excavations commissioned by the NSC found 58 archaeological sites in the park, the adjacent Tainan special industrial zone and Shugu park, spanning roughly 5,000 to 300 years ago.
tension: Rapid land clearance for fabs collided with a 4,500-year record of settlement. Sites were excavated and removed rather than preserved in place.
outcome: NSC and Tainan County proposed a museum in 2002; the Executive Yuan approved NT$1.5 billion in 2007 for what became the Nanke Archaeology Museum.
sources: Ministry of Culture, 南科考古館 article (2010) https://file.moc.gov.tw/001/Upload/OldFiles/AdminUploads/contenthistory/28-5.pdf | PTS, 南科遺跡群 (2024) https://news.pts.org.tw/article/700832

title: High-speed rail vibrations drive fabs away
place: THSR viaduct through the Tainan park
actors: NSC; Bureau of High Speed Rail; Taiwan High Speed Rail Corp.; TSMC; UMC; Winbond; SiS; local residents' self-help group
what: The THSR route was fixed before the park was planned. TSMC said it had been promised vibration at 48 dB at 200 m, unaware the NSC had agreed to 68 dB with the railway. Winbond scrapped a US$3.6 billion 300-mm fab and SiS also withdrew.
tension: Two flagship state projects were planned on the same land without coordination. Tainan County residents formed a self-help group over the vibration problem.
outcome: The railway redesigned the elevated track and the NSC funded vibration-mitigation works. In May 2006 the NSC deputy minister overseeing the parks was detained over contract awards for that work.
sources: EE Times, Rail project puts fabs in limbo (2001) https://www.eetimes.com/?p=1228192 | Taipei Times, NSC vows to help firms (May 2001) https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2001/05/01/0000083960 | IEEE Spectrum, Taiwan's high-tech hubbub (2006) https://spectrum.ieee.org/taiwans-hightech-hubbub

title: Irrigation water from Wushantou redirected to STSP
actors: STSP Administration; Chianan Irrigation Association; Executive Yuan
what: During the 2002–2004 drought, when 65,000 ha were fallowed island-wide, STSP negotiated an agreement to redirect 110,000 m³/day of irrigation water from Wushantou Reservoir.
tension: Agricultural water rights became the reserve supply for the park, setting a template for later droughts.
outcome: Kollar documents at least eight drought reallocations between 2002 and 2023, with fallowing normalised as a tool to shield chip production.
sources: Kollar (2025), Fallowing the fields, feeding the fabs, EPE: Nature and Space https://doi.org/10.1177/25148486251406484

title: Chiayi fallows 43% of farmland while STSP grows
actors: Ministry of Economic Affairs; Council of Agriculture; Chiayi County Magistrate Chang Hua-kuan; Tainan Mayor Lai Ching-te; STSP
what: MOEA suspended irrigation for the first 2015 rice crop. In Chiayi County 7,892 ha, 43% of its farmland, went fallow; Tainan's cuts were lighter. Kollar reports that Mayor Lai approved transfer of Chianan irrigation water to STSP, whose daily use rose from about 200,000 to 250,000 m³ that year.
tension: Chiayi officials called it an unjust allocation and demanded 'water supply justice'; the county was not consulted. Losses also hit seedling suppliers, contract ploughmen and rice millers.
outcome: Compensation went to farmers but the precedent held. Environmental groups argued the park should build its own reclamation instead of competing with farmers.
sources: ETtoday, 張花冠：中央應思供水正義 (Dec 2014) https://www.ettoday.net/news/20141231/445962.htm | The News Lens, 南科用水擴增 (2015) https://www.thenewslens.com/article/12719 | Kollar (2025) https://doi.org/10.1177/25148486251406484

title: Daoye substation fault blacks out Innolux
actors: Taipower; Innolux; TSMC; UMC; ChipMOS
what: Switchgear at the park's Daoye substation failed. Innolux's Tainan fabs 6 and 7 lost power for over three hours and staff were evacuated; TSMC and UMC reported no production impact.
tension: The park's grid is a single point of failure for very large, continuous loads.
outcome: Power restored by noon via backup circuits.
note: Article date not shown in our capture; year inferred from the NCC 2017 plans mentioned in the same report.
sources: Storm Media, 南科大跳電 https://www.storm.mg/article/217062

title: Ciaotou new-town land rezoned as science park
actors: Executive Yuan; MOI Construction & Planning Agency; Kaohsiung City Government; Taisugar
what: Part of the underused Kaohsiung (Ciaotou) New Town was rezoned for a science park. Of the 358 ha, Taisugar held 67% and private owners about 26%; expropriation was estimated at over NT$27 billion. The Executive Yuan approved the park plan in December 2019.
tension: A new town planned for housing failed to fill, so the state repurposed it for industry. Local residents were wait-and-see; an existing legal cosmetics/biotech factory inside the zone said the park was not meant for firms like it.
outcome: The site gained a rare double tax incentive under both the Science Park Act and the New Town Development Act.
note: PTS article date not captured; approval date from Executive Yuan release.
sources: PTS, 南科高雄橋頭園區案 都審會通過 https://news.pts.org.tw/article/452409 | Executive Yuan press release (Sep 2022) https://www.ey.gov.tw/Page/9277F759E41CCD91/a4682dcd-cb0f-40a2-93af-53bedf3ed143

title: Irrigation associations nationalised
actors: Legislative Yuan; Council of Agriculture (now MOA)
what: Authority over irrigation moved from semi-autonomous local irrigation associations to a central MOA agency, during the worst drought in decades.
tension: Kollar argues the reform enabled faster, less contested transfers of irrigation water to science parks and weakened local checks.
outcome: Irrigation districts increasingly operate as auxiliary supply for industry under efficiency-trade agreements financed by chipmakers.
sources: Taipei Times, Legislature nationalizes irrigation groups (Jul 2020) https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2020/07/03/2003739270 | Kollar (2025) https://doi.org/10.1177/25148486251406484

title: 19,385 ha of Chianan rice left dry
actors: Council of Agriculture; MOEA drought centre; Chianan farmers and tenant farmers
what: In the worst drought in decades, the first 2021 rice crop on 19,385 ha of the Zengwen–Wushantou zone was suspended, with compensation of NT$82,000–93,000/ha. Nationwide 74,000 ha were fallowed. Industrial parks were asked to save only 5%.
tension: Compensation went to registered cultivators; tenants on verbal leases had to negotiate with landlords. Officials avoided the word 'fallowing', calling it 'comprehensive water conservation'.
outcome: Kollar reports some fields were permanently abandoned and losses ran into billions of NT$.

title: Contractor cuts 161 kV cable; TSMC Fab 14 P7 dark
actors: Taipower; Wistron NeWeb (new fab construction); TSMC; Innolux; UMC
what: Piling work for a neighbouring tech firm's new plant damaged Taipower's underground 161 kV cable. TSMC Fab 14 P7 ran on diesel generators; industry estimates put the impact at 30,000–60,000 wafers.
tension: Constant construction inside a full park puts the grid that feeds existing fabs at risk.
outcome: Supply switched to another circuit by 4 pm; the contractor's liability was left to investigation.

title: Shanhua land doubles; locals priced out
actors: TSMC; developers; local residents; investors
what: A Tainan realtor said land around Shanhua cost two to three times what it did three or four years earlier. Billboards aimed at 'tech elites' lined the roads at all 14 park entrances.
tension: A Tainan resident described Tainan-born buyers unable to afford flats that outside investors called cheap.
outcome: Prices continued upward through 2023 (see Anding record).

title: Ciaotou EIA: grass owls and organic farmers
actors: Citizen of the Earth Taiwan; Gunshui ecological farming association; Environmental Rights Foundation; STSP Administration; Kaohsiung City
what: NGOs said the site held Eastern grass owls (fewer than 500 left) and the Zhongqi organic farming area, yet no owl compensation plan had been produced. The third review was scheduled less than three weeks after the second.
tension: NGOs said the park faced 'only political deadlines, no industry deadlines', since no tenants were yet confirmed.
outcome: The EIA later passed; the 2026 opening claims retained owl habitat and native trees.
sources: Liberty Times (Jul 2021) https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/life/breakingnews/3616331 | PTS, 橋科環評 https://news.pts.org.tw/article/532731

title: Refinery cleanup cut from 17 years to 3 for TSMC
actors: Kaohsiung City Government; CPC; Environmental Protection Administration; TSMC
what: After TSMC chose the old CPC refinery, remediation moved from CPC to the city and was compressed from 2017–2033 to 2021–2024 using parallel zones. The site had oil-contaminated soil and possible benzene in groundwater.
tension: Legislators questioned how a 17-year cleanup could be done in three. The site exists because the Houjing anti-naphtha-cracker movement forced the refinery's closure in 2015.
outcome: Land handed over in phases; TSMC's 2nm Fab 22 began trial production in 2025.

title: Houjing residents: 'no park this close to homes'
actors: Houjing labour-housing self-help group; Hongyi village chief; CPC retirees; Kaohsiung EPB; TSMC
what: At the Nanzih park EIA reviews, residents bannered for 'housing justice', alleged remediation flaws including wastewater discharged into a drain, and demanded civic monitoring.
tension: The village chief said no other park sits this close to a residential area. TSMC said it would drop the project if it harmed residents.
outcome: The EIA passed preliminary review without a second stage; stricter air monitoring and flood resilience were added.

title: Ciaotou expropriation breaks ground, with ritual relief
actors: Premier Su Tseng-chang; Ministry of the Interior; NSTC; Kaohsiung Mayor Chen Chi-mai; affected landowners and factories
what: Zone expropriation works began across 337.4 ha (NT$12.4 billion). Extra relief beyond statutory compensation included payments for vulnerable households, organic crops, greenhouse rebuilding, and rituals to re-enshrine household deity statues.
tension: The premier framed it as 'two years doing four years' work'; the speed meant displaced factories needed a build-first relocation zone.
outcome: East of Freeway 1 became 185 ha of park; 44 ha west became housing and commerce.

title: Phase III planned on Taisugar's Kanxi farm
actors: Ministry of the Interior; Tainan Urban Development Bureau; STSP; Taisugar
what: With Phases I–II 99% leased, the MOI approved the Phase III urban plan: 84.5 ha mostly on Taisugar's former Kanxi farm, of which 38.9 ha is for factories.
tension: Expansion again depended on converting state sugar farmland.
outcome: TSMC is building new fabs in Phase III, which brokers link to price rises in Shanhua, Xinshi and Guiren.
sources: TechNews (Jan 2023) https://technews.tw/?p=1017344 | Commercial Times (Mar 2026) https://www.ctee.com.tw/news/20260304700184-430602

title: Pingtung wells drilled to supply Kaohsiung
actors: WRA Southern Region Water Resources Office; Pingtung Magistrate Chou Chun-mi; farmers of Ligang, Gaoshu, Jiuru
what: The WRA drilled 28 deep wells in Pingtung, 14 by the Laonong River, to send water to Kaohsiung. One or two hundred farmers bannered at the site; the county said it had not been told the dates.
tension: Farmers feared for irrigation and aquaculture water; Kollar notes Pingtung groundwater had fallen to two-thirds of norms and warns of subsidence.
outcome: Work paused for local consultation; the WRA apologised for skipping explanation.

title: Park water allegedly booked as 'residential'
actors: STSP; WRA; TaiSounds reporter Hong
what: Reporting cited by Kollar alleged that southern science parks drew on residential supply lines, hiding industrial demand from public scrutiny while farmers lost irrigation.
tension: Accounting categories shape what scarcity looks like in official statistics.
outcome: Unresolved; treat as a reported allegation.
note: Allegation from media, relayed by an academic source. Not independently verified here.

title: First full-year fallow in Chianan
actors: WRA; MOA Irrigation Agency; rice farmers; seedling suppliers, millers
what: With Zengwen Reservoir at 10.6% in April 2023, the WRA ordered 47,000 ha in Chianan fallowed across both rice seasons, Taiwan's first full-year fallow.
tension: Farmers demanded 'give back our right to work'; ripple losses hit seedling, milling and labour supply chains.
outcome: Kollar argues this deepened long-term decline of smallholder rice farming.
sources: FoodNext (Apr 2023) https://www.foodnext.net/issue/paper/5098803525 | Kollar (2025) https://doi.org/10.1177/25148486251406484

title: Fenghua substation fault hits two parks
actors: Taipower; UMC; TSMC; memory, panel and test firms
what: A 161 kV GIS disconnect switch failed at Taipower's Fenghua substation, causing voltage dips in the Tainan and Kaohsiung parks and a 6-minute outage for 28,159 households. UMC reported damaged wafers.
tension: Grid reliability is now a production input; a test firm scrapped in-process products.
outcome: Supply restored the same afternoon.
note: Substation location not verified; plotted at the Tainan park.
sources: Liberty Times (Jun 2023) https://ec.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/4320687

title: 'A monster that eats power and water'
actors: Houjing residents; NCKU Prof. Chen Hsiu-ling; Kaohsiung Economic Development Bureau; TSMC
what: When TSMC switched the Nanzih fab to 2nm, residents at the hearing said CPC had finally left only for an electricity- and water-eating monster to arrive, and asked whether homes would face shortages. Residents cited over 700 cancer cases in Houjing.
tension: The city said TSMC would use about 40,000 t/day, covered by 100,000 t of subsurface water and 105,000 t of reclaimed water from Ciaotou and Nanzih plants.
outcome: A health risk assessment was added to the EIA-difference review.
sources: PTS (Aug 2023) https://news.pts.org.tw/article/651311 | CNA (Aug 2023) https://www.cna.com.tw/news/afe/202308140289.aspx

title: Anding farmland jumps tenfold
actors: Expropriated landowners; Anding Farmers' Association; Yungching Realty
what: Resale prices in Anding rose 88.2% in five years (Xinshi 80.7%). Farmland went from NT$4–5 million to 40–50 million per fen. The farmers' association's deposits grew from NT$2 billion to 9.5 billion over 20 years.
tension: Expropriation made some elderly owners suddenly rich, described as about 200 'grandparents' who live quietly as hidden millionaires, while farming land vanished.
outcome: Anding became the fastest-rising district around any science park.
sources: NOWnews (2024) https://www.nownews.com/news/6421447

title: TSMC picks Chiayi; housing rises from empty fields
actors: TSMC; Chiayi County Government; developer Ching Ching Lin
what: TSMC announced two advanced-packaging fabs on about 20 ha of the 88 ha Chiayi Science Park (groundbreaking May 2023). Taibao pre-sale prices rose from NT$261k to 284k per ping.
tension: A developer recalled that when he launched his first HSR-area project in 2021 there was nothing around, the grass was taller than him, and staff ate at the station's convenience store. Even locals doubted it.
outcome: The developer has over 2,000 units in Taibao; one project is branded 'AI World City'.

title: Burials found under TSMC Chiayi fab
actors: TSMC; NTU archaeology team; Chiayi County Cultural Affairs Bureau; Beishi village residents
what: Excavation for the first fab hit a cord-marked pottery site over 1,000 years old, with pottery and 10+ human burials including children. The dig recruited 60 workers at NT$1,700/day; villagers said farm labour already paid 1,500–1,600.
tension: After a string of construction accidents in 2025, local talk linked them to the disturbed graves; archaeologists asked people not to demonise the work.
outcome: The county reordered construction so the excavation would not delay tool move-in.

title: Ciaotou access road: one farmer's third expropriation
actors: Kaohsiung City Government; affected farmers and factory owners
what: The Tai-39 extension along the HSR line required more land. A 67-year-old farmer whose plot sits under the rail faced his third expropriation and said less than one fen would not support a living.
tension: Owners called the timeline too short to relocate and compensation too low to buy equal land.
outcome: The city promised negotiated purchase and help finding industrial land.
sources: PTS (2024) https://news.pts.org.tw/article/688227

title: 531 ha Shalun farm approved as STSP Phase IV
actors: National Development Council; NSTC; STSP Administration; Taisugar; tenant melon farmers
what: The NDC approved the Shalun Ecological Science Park: 531 ha, NT$122.7 billion, 35,000 jobs, aimed at AI and HPC demand. The land is a Taisugar farm now growing watermelons.
tension: A tenant farmer said leases were one year at a time, rent was not cheap, and now the state could take it back at will.
outcome: EIA began in 2026; the park would bring the Tainan campus to about 1,600 ha.

title: Grass owls vs. the AI park
actors: Wild Bird Federation; Tainan Wild Bird Society; STSP Director Cheng; TSMC; NSTC
what: Bird groups said Shalun is the easiest place in Taiwan to see the Eastern grass owl and holds 35 protected species. They refused one-on-one meetings and asked for a joint platform.
tension: Groups said '175 ha of grass, green and water' would mostly be parks and detention ponds, not owl habitat.
outcome: A third-party ecological collaboration platform was set up in late 2025, with 18 ha of offset habitat on the Erren River floodplain.

title: 375 ha expropriation, 2,000+ landowners
actors: Tainan Land Administration Bureau; Mayor Huang Wei-che; Ministry of the Interior; 2,000+ landowners; developers
what: Tainan's largest ever land development: zone expropriation of 375.22 ha across Shanhua, Xinshi and Anding, approved by MOI on 22 Oct 2025. Owners could take cash or return land (抵價地). Cheques were handed out at a sugar culture park.

outcome: Includes 159 ha for housing and commerce, intended to fix the area's thin services.

title: Commuter jams spill into village lanes
actors: Tainan Public Works and Transport Bureaus; Hucuoliao residents; park commuters
what: Commuters called the park end of Xingangshe Avenue a 'giant parking disaster'. Traffic from Madou and Jiali cut through Hucuoliao's lanes and levee roads at rush hour.
tension: The park's workforce lives far from it, so daily life around it is organised by the commute.
outcome: A NT$1 billion road widening began in 2025; AI traffic signals cut morning delay by about 14 minutes.
note: Exact location of Hucuoliao not verified; plotted at Anding district level.

title: Ciaotou opens: 'industry east, homes west'
actors: Ministry of the Interior; Kaohsiung City; STSP Administration; 26 tenant firms
what: The park opened with industry east of the freeway and housing, schools and services west, explicitly to avoid older zones that had 'only industry, no life'.
tension: Planners themselves named the problem of industrial zones that are workplaces with nowhere to live.

title: 1,000 ha Shalun rezoning withdrawn under protest
actors: Tainan City Government; MOI National Land Planning Committee; Monitoring Governance Alliance; Earth Heart Environmental Association
what: Tainan proposed reclassifying over 1,000 ha of Shalun farmland from Agriculture-2 to urban development, beyond the 531 ha park. NGOs called it land speculation by zoning; the city withdrew.
tension: Groups said the city was treating farmland protection under the National Spatial Plan as a formality.
outcome: MOI reminded the city that zoning is not permission to develop.

title: Nanzih and Shalun: 'TSMC uses up Kaohsiung's power'
actors: Citizen of the Earth Taiwan; Ministry of Environment; STSP; TSMC
what: For five 2nm fabs at Nanzih, NGOs estimated 11.2 billion kWh a year, equal to Kaohsiung's residential and commercial use. Adding Shalun (supplied from Hsinta) gives about 20.1 billion kWh, close to Kaohsiung's total.

what: At groundbreaking of a 28 ha TSMC-led supplier zone, Wei said a month earlier TSMC was worried about water and considered trucking it in; rain and planned reservoir links reassured him. Talent was now the bigger worry.
tension: The southernmost node of the S-Corridor depends on water transfers in a county already pumping groundwater.
outcome: Construction under way.

title: 'Richest village, no shopping mall'
actors: Tainan City Council; village chiefs; park engineers; developers
what: Shanhua's Liantan village has Tainan's highest average income (NT$2.345 million). Engineers used to live in Tainan city; more now live nearby but find no matching services: 'wallets full, but the area hasn't caught up'.
tension: An Anding village chief said his district had been 'disappeared' while investment went to Shanhua and Xinshi. Netizens said park staff would rather buy in Yongkang or Annan.

title: Luzhu rezones 49.9 ha of farmland
actors: Kaohsiung Urban Planning Commission; Deputy Mayor Lin Chin-rong; landowners
what: About 49.9 ha of agricultural zone was approved for zone expropriation into industrial, residential and commercial land as a support base for Ciaotou and the S-Corridor.
tension: The city said the land no longer fitted farm use; about 70% of owners supported inclusion.

actors: Solar developers; landowners; aquaculture farmers; MOEA Energy Administration
what: An 88-round shooting in Xuejia during the 2022 local elections exposed conflict over land assembly for fishery-solar (漁電共生) projects in coastal Tainan.
